identity.title: The multiphase gas structure and kinematics in the circumnuclear region of NGC 5728
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report on our combined analysis of HST, VLT/MUSE, VLT/SINFONI, and ALMA observations of the local Seyfert 2 galaxy, NGC 5728 to investigate in detail the feeding and feedback of the AGN.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit single-Gaussian emission lines per spaxel

method.value: Single Gaussians to CO(2-1) and optical/NIR lines; errors from 100 Monte Carlo perturbed spectra using line-free RMS

evidence.quote: we produced 100 simulated spectra for every emission line by randomly perturbing the original spectra assuming a Gaussian distribution with a standard deviation equal to the RMS

fitting.value: Single Gaussian least squares; doublet ratios fixed to 3

evidence.quote: fixed the intensity ratio to the expected theoretical value of 3 for the \[OIII\] and \[NII\] doublets

method.value: Integrate CO(2-1) within 6.5'' aperture over +/-375 km/s, convert to L'CO and mass

evidence.quote: we simply integrated the spectrum between rest-frame velocities of $\pm375$ km s$^{-1}$ to obtain a total CO (2–1) intensity ($S_{\rm C O}$) of 93.6 Jy km s$^{-1}$
we use $\alpha_{\scriptscriptstyle \rm CO} = 1.1$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ pc$^{-2}$/(K km s$^{-2}$)

findings_qualitative.value: CO(2-1) holes along the NLR bicone coexist with strong ionized gas; interpreted as either lack of molecular gas or CO suppression by X-rays

evidence.quote: A plausible explanation for these holes is instead that CO (2–1) is not accurately tracing the presence molecular gas in the NLR.

claims.hypothesis: Is the circumnuclear ring a rotating star-forming disk?
claims.experiment: DYSMALPY disk fits to CO and stellar velocity fields
claims.result: CO i=43.3 deg, stars i=42.1 deg; residuals <40 km/s in stars
claims.finding: The ring is a rotating disk with young stars born from the molecular gas

evidence.quote: the good agreement between the models and the data as well as between the cold molecular gas and the stars indicates that our interpretation of a rotating circumnuclear ring is correct

claims.hypothesis: Is there molecular gas structure inside the ring that feeds the AGN?
claims.experiment: MultiNest multi-component fits to CO(2-1) in the central 4''
claims.result: Three kinematic components (~40%, 40%, 20% of nuclear gas)
claims.finding: Ring-like rotation, a warped inner disk, and gas along the nuclear bar

evidence.quote: Our analysis therefore suggests the presence of three kinematically distinct cold molecular gas components in the nuclear region of NGC 5728.

claims.hypothesis: Is the AGN driving a strong ionized outflow that disrupts the circumnuclear region?
claims.experiment: Bicone modelling of [SiVI] and Brgamma-based energetics
claims.result: Peak Mdot 0.08 Msun/yr, 0.003% of L_Bol, momentum ratio 0.043
claims.finding: Weak, momentum-driven outflow, consistent with Fiore scaling relations; not disrupting the region

evidence.quote: These properties all suggest that the outflow currently is not energy driven but rather momentum driven given their extremely low values

claims.hypothesis: Do CO holes mean the AGN removed molecular gas?
claims.experiment: Compare CO holes with ionized and H2 emission
claims.result: Holes are filled with ionized gas
claims.finding: Holes may reflect CO suppression/missing gas rather than clear evacuation; unresolved without higher-J CO

evidence.quote: To confirm the lack of molecular gas in the NLR, however, observations of higher-J CO lines are needed.

why_this_data.value: Multiwavelength IFU and ALMA data probe stars, ionized and molecular gas at matched spatial scales

evidence.quote: it is now possible to study simultaneously the distribution and kinematics of both ionized and molecular gas at the same spatial scales in an efficient manner

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Spike in excitation diagram explained by A_M/I or by ionization parameter; they chose the simpler increase in U

evidence.quote: we choose the simpler increase in $U$ model as our explanation

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA lacks short spacings; diffuse flux resolved out, so mass is a lower limit

evidence.quote: an indication that diffuse flux was resolved out due to the lack of short spacings during the ALMA observation

limitations_admitted.value: Disk model errors are statistical only

evidence.quote: the very small errors on the model parameters only incorporate the statistical uncertainties

referee_caveats_inferred: Single ALMA pointing with limited resolution (0.5'') and no short spacings; CO-to-H2 factor assumed
Molecular inflow/outflow from velocity residuals is sensitive to the disk model and non-circular orbits
Ionized outflow mass depends on assumed constant ne (1550 cm^-3) and projection corrections
Five-to-three component grouping of CO components is subjective

data_public_as_stated.value: Archival ALMA, MUSE-DEEP (ESO Phase 3), and HST (MAST) data downloaded; SINFONI from program 093.B-0057

evidence.quote: We downloaded archival MUSE data of NGC 5728 from the MUSE-DEEP collection, an ESO Phase 3 data release

missing_for_reproduction: Reduced SINFONI and X-Shooter cubes (LLAMA) not clearly public

Exact CASA calibration and imaging parameters
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB for ALMA raw data; MUSE and HST cubes several GB
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA imaging and disk fitting are fairly specified, but multi-instrument data, unreleased code and missing parameters limit full reproduction.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key results depend on non-ALMA datasets and unreleased fitting tools, and many settings are unstated.
